content.title: Recommendations (selected items)

recommendations.notes: Plasma natriuretic peptides recommended as initial diagnostic tests in patients with symptoms suggestive of heart failure.

recommendations.item: Routine blood tests for comorbidities (including full blood count, urea and electrolytes, thyroid function, fasting glucose and HbA1c, lipids, iron status [TSAT and ferritin])

content.section_4.2_natriuretic_peptides_summary: Plasma concentrations of natriuretic peptides (NPs) are recommended as initial diagnostic tests in patients with symptoms suggestive of heart failure (HF) to rule out the diagnosis. Elevated NP concentrations support a diagnosis of HF, are useful for prognostication and may guide further cardiac investigation. Many causes (both cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular) can elevate NP and reduce diagnostic accuracy (examples noted: atrial fibrillation, increasing age, acute or chronic kidney disease). Conversely, NP concentrations may be disproportionately low in obese patients.
